course.title: Presentation Skills
course.tagline: Present ideas clearly with slides and words that keep people listening.

days.title: What makes a good presentation?
days.goal: Say what makes a presentation work.
steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about what makes a good presentation: one message, clear slides, calm speaker you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises what makes a good presentation: one message, clear slides, calm speaker.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using what makes a good presentation: one message, clear slides, calm speaker, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Watch a short talk online and write down three things that worked.
days.challenge: Tell a friend what makes a presentation good, in one minute.

quiz.q: What does every good presentation need?
options: One clear message.
Fifty slides.
Tiny text on every slide.
A joke every minute.
quiz.explain: Every good presentation has one clear message. Everything else supports it.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Build a full slide deck for a three-minute talk.
Say what makes a presentation work.
Answer questions calmly and honestly.
Give your talk to a small group of real people.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about What makes a good presentation? — its goal is: Say what makes a presentation work.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: strong openings: a question, a story or a fact
using your body: posture, movement and gestures
timing your talk
what makes a good presentation: one message, clear slides, calm speaker
quiz.explain: Today's focus was what makes a good presentation: one message, clear slides, calm speaker.

options: Pick the most important one and save the rest.

Build or revise one slide that practises presenting with a partner.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using presenting with a partner, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Plan a short talk with a partner: who says what.
days.challenge: Give the talk together and hand over smoothly.

quiz.q: What makes a good handover between partners?
options: A clear line like 'Now Ada will show you the next part.'
Just stopping and staring.
Talking over each other.
Leaving the room.
quiz.explain: A clear handover line keeps the talk smooth. Plan who says what before you start.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Share a presentation with a partner.
Give a short presentation in a real setting.
Pick one main message for your presentation.
Use a picture to say what words cannot.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Present with a partner — its goal is: Share a presentation with a partner.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: recovering from mistakes in a talk
presenting anywhere with confidence
presenting with a partner
simple slides: one idea, big words, few words
quiz.explain: Today's focus was presenting with a partner.

days.title: Your five-minute talk
days.goal: Give a five-minute presentation from start to finish.

video.title: How to Prepare for a Presentation

steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about a full five-minute presentation you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises a full five-minute presentation.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using a full five-minute presentation, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Give your five-minute talk with slides to a small group.
days.challenge: Time it and keep it between four and six minutes.

quiz.q: How long should you practise before a five-minute talk?
options: Practise out loud at least three times.
Once in your head is enough.
Never practise, just be natural.
Practise for five hours only.
quiz.explain: Practise out loud at least three times. Practice is what makes a talk feel natural.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Make a deck that looks clean and professional.
Give a five-minute presentation from start to finish.
Shape your presentation for your listeners.
Talk to people, not to your slides.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Your five-minute talk — its goal is: Give a five-minute presentation from start to finish.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: persuading with slides
what makes a good presentation: one message, clear slides, calm speaker
building a full slide deck
a full five-minute presentation
quiz.explain: Today's focus was a full five-minute presentation.

project.title: The Five-Minute Talk
project.brief: Give a five-minute presentation with a clean deck to a small group. Time it and ask the group what was clear and what was not.
checks: Your talk lasted four to six minutes
Your deck looks clean: one font, two colours
You had one clear main message
You looked at your listeners
You handled at least one question
You asked the group for feedback

days.title: Use numbers well
days.goal: Use numbers so people understand them.
steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about using numbers people can understand you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises using numbers people can understand.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using using numbers people can understand, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Rewrite three big numbers as simple comparisons.
days.challenge: Explain a number in your talk with a simple picture.

quiz.q: Why do big numbers confuse people?
options: People cannot picture them. A simple comparison helps.
Numbers are always boring.
People hate maths.
Numbers should never be used.
quiz.explain: People cannot picture big numbers. 'As big as three football fields' helps more than a raw number.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Watch yourself and pick two things to improve.
Plan a presentation in three parts.
Use numbers so people understand them.
Change your speed, volume and tone.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Use numbers well — its goal is: Use numbers so people understand them.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: using numbers people can understand
presenting at work or school
picking one main message
using pictures instead of walls of text
quiz.explain: Today's focus was using numbers people can understand.

days.title: Present online
days.goal: Present well on a video call.
steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about presenting on a video call you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises presenting on a video call.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using presenting on a video call, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Record a two-minute talk on video and watch it back.
days.challenge: Give a short talk on a video call with a friend.

quiz.q: What matters most when presenting online?
options: Look at the camera, speak clearly and check your slides share well.
Wear a suit.
Use ten slides per minute.
Turn your camera off.
quiz.explain: Look at the camera, speak clearly and make sure your slides share well. That is most of online presenting.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Give your best five-minute presentation so far.
Start your presentation with a hook.
Stand tall, move with purpose and use gestures.
Present well on a video call.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Present online — its goal is: Present well on a video call.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: designing a clean deck
presenting on a video call
knowing your listeners
speaking, not reading your slides
quiz.explain: Today's focus was presenting on a video call.

days.title: Recover from mistakes
days.goal: Keep going calmly when something goes wrong.
steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about recovering from mistakes in a talk you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises recovering from mistakes in a talk.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using recovering from mistakes in a talk, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Practise your talk, then drop your notes and keep going.
days.challenge: Give a talk and recover from one planned mistake.

quiz.q: What should you do if you lose your place?
options: Pause, breathe, find your next point and go on.
Panic and run off.
Say sorry five times.
Start the whole talk again.
quiz.explain: Pause, breathe, find your next point and go on. Listeners forget small slips fast.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Keep going calmly when something goes wrong.
Present with confidence in any room.
Make slides with one idea each.
Use eye contact to connect with the room.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Recover from mistakes — its goal is: Keep going calmly when something goes wrong.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: reviewing your own talks
planning a talk: opening, body, closing
recovering from mistakes in a talk
using your voice: speed, volume and tone
quiz.explain: Today's focus was recovering from mistakes in a talk.

days.title: Persuade with slides
days.goal: Use your presentation to persuade people.
steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about persuading with slides you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises persuading with slides.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using persuading with slides, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Write a one-minute talk that asks people to do one thing.
days.challenge: Persuade a friend to try something new, with one slide.

quiz.q: What persuades people best?
options: A clear reason plus a real example.
Shouting louder than others.
Using hard words.
Talking for a very long time.
quiz.explain: A clear reason plus a real example persuades people. Shouting never does.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Say what makes a presentation work.
Use your presentation to persuade people.
Build a full slide deck for a three-minute talk.
Answer questions calmly and honestly.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Persuade with slides — its goal is: Use your presentation to persuade people.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: your best talk: message, story, voice, slides
strong openings: a question, a story or a fact
using your body: posture, movement and gestures
persuading with slides
quiz.explain: Today's focus was persuading with slides.

days.task: Offer to present for two minutes in your next meeting or class.
days.challenge: Present in a real meeting or class today.

quiz.q: What helps most at work or school talks?
options: One clear point and short sentences.
Long words and long sentences.
Reading from your phone.
Talking without a point.
quiz.explain: One clear point and short sentences work best at work or school.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Pick one main message for your presentation.
Use a picture to say what words cannot.
Give a short presentation in a real setting.
Use a short true story to make a point.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Present at work or school — its goal is: Give a short presentation in a real setting.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: presenting at work or school
presenting anywhere with confidence
simple slides: one idea, big words, few words
eye contact with listeners
quiz.explain: Today's focus was presenting at work or school.

steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about designing a clean deck you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises designing a clean deck.

Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Redesign your deck: one font, two colours, lots of white space.
days.challenge: Show your deck to a friend. Ask what looks messy.

quiz.q: What makes a deck look clean?
options: One font, two colours and lots of empty space.
Five fonts and ten colours.
A picture on every inch.
Tiny text everywhere.
quiz.explain: One font, two colours and lots of empty space make a deck look clean and professional.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Shape your presentation for your listeners.
Talk to people, not to your slides.
End your presentation so people remember it.
Make a deck that looks clean and professional.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Design a clean deck — its goal is: Make a deck that looks clean and professional.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: what makes a good presentation: one message, clear slides, calm speaker
designing a clean deck
building a full slide deck
answering questions from listeners
quiz.explain: Today's focus was designing a clean deck.

options: What was clear and what needs fixing.
Only what was bad.
Only what was good.
Nothing, never watch yourself.
quiz.explain: Look for what was clear and what needs fixing. Both help you grow.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Watch yourself and pick two things to improve.
Plan a presentation in three parts.
Change your speed, volume and tone.
Practise your presentation out loud until it feels natural.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Review your talks — its goal is: Watch yourself and pick two things to improve.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: picking one main message
using pictures instead of walls of text
reviewing your own talks
telling a short true story in a talk
quiz.explain: Today's focus was reviewing your own talks.

days.title: Your best talk yet
days.goal: Give your best five-minute presentation so far.
steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about your best talk: message, story, voice, slides you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises your best talk: message, story, voice, slides.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using your best talk: message, story, voice, slides, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.

days.challenge: Ask the group to rate your talk from 1 to 10 and say why.

quiz.q: What makes a talk your best yet?
options: A clear message, honest feeling and good practice.
Perfect words with no mistakes.
The longest talk you ever gave.
The most jokes you ever told.
quiz.explain: A clear message, honest feeling and good practice make your best talk. Perfection is not the goal.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Start your presentation with a hook.
Give your best five-minute presentation so far.
Stand tall, move with purpose and use gestures.
Keep your talk inside its time limit.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Your best talk yet — its goal is: Give your best five-minute presentation so far.

speaking, not reading your slides

your best talk: message, story, voice, slides

steps: Watch today's video and note the one idea about presenting anywhere with confidence you will use in your own slides.
Build or revise one slide that practises presenting anywhere with confidence.
Rehearse a 2-minute talk using presenting anywhere with confidence, standing up and timing yourself.
Record the rehearsal and fix the weakest slide or sentence.
Present the talk to one real person today and ask what was clearest.
days.task: Give a two-minute talk in a place you have never presented before.
days.challenge: Present in a new place today without preparing.

quiz.q: What is the mark of a confident presenter?
options: They can present clearly in any room, even unprepared.
They never feel nervous.
They never make mistakes.
They always read from notes.
quiz.explain: A confident presenter can present clearly in any room. Nerves still come, but they do not stop them.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Make slides with one idea each.
Use eye contact to connect with the room.
Present with confidence in any room.
Calm your nerves before you present.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Present anywhere — its goal is: Present with confidence in any room.

options: presenting anywhere with confidence
planning a talk: opening, body, closing
using your voice: speed, volume and tone
practising out loud, not in your head

capstone.title: The Confident Presenter
capstone.brief: Give a five-minute presentation with slides to a real audience of at least five people. Pick one clear message, open strong, tell one story, and close with one thing for people to do. Record it.
checks: You had one clear main message
You opened with a hook
You told one short true story
Your slides had one idea each
You spoke slowly with pauses
You handled questions calmly
You recorded the talk and wrote down two things to improve
deliverables: A video recording of your five-minute presentation
A one-page plan of the talk: message, opening, three points, closing
A list of feedback from at least three listeners
A short note on what you will improve next
